preamble: Devoicing of the bilabial implosive to [p]. In the Pearic languages Chong and Pear, Proto-Austroasiatic *ɓ appears as p (*ɓic 'to lie down, sleep' > Chong pìc, Pear pic), where Katuic keeps b (Bru bếq). Headley (1985) reconstructs Proto-Pearic *buːl 'drunk' with *b, and the step Proto-Pearic *b > p is filed under b > p. In Southern Kam (Kam-Sui), Proto-Kam-Sui *ɓun¹ 'sky' appears as benl /pən⁵⁵/, where Sui qbenl keeps the preglottalized stop. Khmer reached p in two attested steps: Proto-Austroasiatic *ɓaːr 'two' > Old Khmer ពិរ៑ bir > Modern Khmer ពីរ /piː/. These are filed under ɓ > b and b > p. Modern Khmer ɓ and ɗ are secondary, from earlier *p and *t (បី 'three' < Old Khmer ⟨pi⟩ [ɓiː] < *peːʔ; ដៃ 'hand' < *t₁iiʔ), so the two series swapped places.
phoneticEffects: Devoicing, Loss of Implosion, Airstream Change

examples.note: Sui qbenl keeps the preglottalized stop /ʔb/. Compare Proto-Tai *ɓɯnᴬ (Thai บน). The sources consulted give only this one example.
